approach: Narrative review of randomised clinical trials. The authors selected trials evaluating the concomitant administration of ICIs and chemotherapy to assess outcomes such as overall survival, objective response rates, and safety profiles. The review synthesizes these results to highlight synergistic effects and identify gaps in current evidence, particularly regarding treatment sequencing.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Summarizes the clinical rationale and trial data supporting the synergy between chemotherapy and ICIs in specific solid tumour types (e.g., NSCLC).
contribution_and_limits.limits: The provided abstract does not detail the systematic search strategy, inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond 'randomised clinical trials', or specific statistical methods if any meta-analysis was performed. It focuses on concomitant administration and notes the lack of head-to-head comparisons for sequential strategies.

key_findings.conditions: First-line treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and PD-1/PD-L1 enriched tumours
key_findings.finding: Improved overall survival and better objective response rates compared to standard chemotherapy alone, suggesting a potential synergistic effect.
Improved survival results raise questions about the optimal approach between sequential and concomitant administration of chemoimmunotherapy.
Improved Progression Free Survival 2 (PFS2), suggesting a potential long-lasting effect of ICIs when used in combination in the first-line setting.

key_findings.conditions: General safety profile across tested combinations
key_findings.finding: No new safety signals were found with the combination tested to date.

problem_or_question: To assess the clinical efficacy and safety profiles of combining ICIs with chemotherapy in advanced solid tumours, and to evaluate the rationale behind using chemotherapy to enhance ICI effectiveness.
research_scope: Advanced solid tumours, specifically focusing on the combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with standard chemotherapy. The review covers randomised clinical trials evaluating concomitant administration.
work_summary: This paper reviews the rationale and clinical evidence for combining ICIs (anti-PD-1/PD-L1) with chemotherapy in advanced solid tumours. It addresses why this combination is used (chemotherapy's potential to enhance immunogenicity or break resistance), summarizes findings from randomised trials regarding efficacy and safety, and discusses emerging questions about treatment sequencing (concomitant vs. sequential).
